For a soy sauce substitute that maintains the savory, umami profile of a stir-fry while being soy-free, coconut aminos are the best option. They have a similar salty and slightly sweet flavor profile, though they are less salty than traditional soy sauce, so you may want to adjust the quantity slightly or add a pinch of salt. Another alternative is tamari if the allergy is strictly to soy proteins but not gluten, but since the allergy is to soy, coconut aminos are the safer bet. You can also use a mixture of beef or mushroom broth with a little balsamic vinegar or molasses to mimic the depth of flavor.
